Since the installation instructions for face-ripper-9000 isn't entirely clear and a lot of you seem to be having difficulty getting it running, I figured I'd write out a more in-depth tutorial that's hopefully a little easier to follow. Unfortunately at the moment this is a Mac tutorial only, but when I get some more time I'll come back and add a PC version as well. I've dumbed it down a fair bit to make it accessible to as many people as possible so I apologize if it comes across as patronizing to any veteran coders reading this.

Installing dependencies

For those who don't code, a dependency is exactly what it sounds like. It's something a program depends on to be able to run properly, so obviously we need to install everything below to get face-ripper running. If you've never used a command line before this might look intimidating, but you'll just be copy/pasting code, so don't freak out.

Homebrew

Not technically a dependency, but it'll make your life a lot easier, so we're going to install it anyway. Homebrew has Apple's X-Code as it's own dependency, so we're going to have to install that first. The easiest way to do this is to just open up the app store, search for 'xcode' and install the first option that pops up. It might take a while to download. Once it's finished, open it up, accept the license terms and conditions, then close it again.

Now we're going to open up the program 'Terminal' which you can find in "Applications > Utilities > Terminal". In window that pops up, you're going to run (type in, then press enter) the command xcode-select --install. If it starts installing, let it run until it's finished. Run the command again to make sure you're getting the following message: xcode-select: error: command line tools are already installed, use "Software Update" to install updates you're ready to move on.

In the same terminal window, run /usr/bin/ruby -e "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/master/install)" which should install the latest version of Homebrew on your computer. If you already had it installed, run brew update to make sure you're not using an outdated version.

Python

Chances are you already have a version of python installed on your computer, but version 2.7.10 (which is installed by default) won't work for this, so we need to install python 3. To do this, in the same terminal window, just run brew python3. Once it's done, run python3 --version. If it prints out Python 3.6.4 you're ready to move on to the next step.

NumPy

In the same terminal window, run pip3 install numpy.

Cmake

In the same terminal window, run brew install cmake.

OpenCV

In the same terminal window, enter pip3 install scipy matplotlib scikit-image scikit-learn ipython pandas OpenCV claims it requires these dependencies to work, but I actually only ever installed NumPy and it worked fine for me, but install them anyway just to be safe. Once they've finished installing, in the same terminal window enter brew install opencv3 --with-contrib --with-python3.

Before we move on, let's test that OpenCV installed correctly. In your terminal window, type python3 to enter the python interpreter. Now type import cv2 and press enter, then type cv2.__version__ and press enter. If it prints out '3.4.0' or a higher version, you've installed OpenCV correctly. Exit the interpreter by clicking Control + Z.

Dlib

In your terminal window, enter pip3 install dlib. When it's done, test it's installed correctly by re-entering the python interpreter with python3 then type import dlib and press enter, then type dlib.__version__ and press enter. If it prints out '19.9.0' or a higher version, you've installed dlib correctly. Exit the interpreter by clicking Control + Z

face_recognition

In your terminal window, type pip3 install face_recognition.

If you followed all the steps correctly, you should now be ready to install face-ripper-9000!

Setting up Face-Ripper-9000

First thing you'll want to do is download the code. Go to this link, and click the green button that says 'Clone or Download'. If you know how to use git, go ahead and clone it as per usual, but to keep it simple for the tutorial, we're going to select 'Download Zip'.

Once it's finished downloading, open up your zip file and extract everything in it to a folder of your choice. As an example, I'm going to pretend I extracted it to ~/Development/deepfakes/face-ripper-9000. It doesn't matter where you extract it, so long as you remember the path to the folder. Within this folder, create a new folder called 'vids'.

Now you're going to collect a set of videos containing the person who's face you want to extract. There are other guides on this, but usually I just download interview videos from youtube. Make sure that they're either mp4 or mkv format. Once you have your videos, move them into the 'vids' folder you just created. The final step before you run your program is to find a high quality photo of your target person's face, download it, and save it in your face-ripper-9000 folder as 'pic.jpg'

Using Face-Ripper-9000

Now that you have your picture and folder full of videos, you're ready to use the program. Bring up your terminal window, and navigate to your face-ripper folder by entering cd /path/to/faceripper/folder, (so in my case I'd enter cd ~/Development/deepfakes/face-ripper-9000).

To start up the program, you're going to enter the following: python3 demo.py -i 'path/to/your/image/pic.jpg' -v 'path/to/your/vids/folder'. So in my case I'd enter python3 demo.py -i '~/Development/deepfakes/face-ripper-9000/pic.jpg' -v '~/Development/deepfakes/face-ripper-9000/vids'

If you did everything correctly, face-ripper should now start combing through your videos and outputting face frames to a new folder called 'pic_output' that will automatically be created in your face-ripper-9000 directory.

If you want to play around with the settings, you can add 'arguments' to your input that will change the program parametres. As an example of how arguments are used, the -i argument we used above will take whatever follows it and use it as the path for your input image, and the -v argument will take whatever follows it as the path for your video folder.

-i and -v are the only required arguments. If you don't manually enter the following arguments, they'll just use their default values.

Argument Explanation Default Value
-t Tolerance of face detection, lower is stricter (0.1-1.0) 0.6
-f Amount of frames per second to scan. 25
-n Number photos of the face to extract from each video. 1000
-s Minimum KB size of images to keep in the faceset. 32

So if I wanted to run the program with a loose tolerance of 0.3, that scans 10 frame per second, that extracts a maximum of 500 frames per video, and that removes any images with a file size lower than 40kb, I'd enter something like this:

~/Development/deepfakes/face-ripper-9000/pic.jpg' -v '~/Development/deepfakes/face-ripper-9000/vids' -t 0.3 -f 10 -n 500 -s 40

Again, if you run into any problems, or you have any questions, just leave a comment below and I'll do my best to help out/ammend the tutorial.
